To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the mechanical and viscoelastic properties of epoxy systems based on the digylcidyl ether of the bisphenol A cured with mixtures of aliphatic and cycloaliphatics diamine are strongly influenced by the stoichiometry and by the cure conditions.

the glass transition temperatures of the cured systems were higher than those of the unreacted systems, and the flexural properties were improved by the use of stoichiometric ratios of 1:1 and higher, and by the use of postcure schedules.
stoichiometric ratios, cure conditions, and the chemical composition of the amine mixture affect the viscoelastic and mechanical behavior of the cured epoxy systems.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of stoichiometry, cure schedule, and post-cure on the viscoelastic and flexural properties of epoxy networks based on a mixture of an amine and a diamine.

the study of the influence of stoichiometric ratio and cure conditions on the viscoelastic properties and mechanical behaviour of DGEBA-based systems with a mixture of aliphatic triamines and cycloaliphatics diamines.
the effect of stoichiometry on the mechanical and viscoelastic properties of epoxy systems cured at different temperatures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the glass transition temperatures of the mixtures with different ratios were not affected by the cure schedule.
, as expected, the glass transition temperature increases with the degree of crosslinking, and the mechanical properties increase with the crosslink density.
the glass transition temperatures are not only a function of the crosslink density, but also of the molecular mobility of the polymer chain.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the glass transition temperature increases with the stoichiometric ratio and the crosslink density, and decreases when the cure is not complete.
the mechanical properties are not only influenced by crosslink density but also by the chemical structure of the network, and by the cure schedule.
the glass transition temperatures of the cured mixtures are correlated to the stoichiometry and the degree of conversion of the systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the glass transition temperature and the flexural properties of the cured systems are strongly dependent on the stoichiometry.
the glass transition temperature is not the only parameter that determines the mechanical properties of the cured systems.

a mixture of an amine with different chemical structure and functionalities, such as the one used in our work, can be used to control the glass transition temperature, crosslink density, and mechanical properties of DGEBA-based epoxy networks.
